_doc: T21b scoring spec, derived by hand from eval/realworld/oracle/<id>.json at bc71082 (the oracle files are not edited). A pair = two sides A and B, each a list of alternative sites [file-pattern (fnmatch on the basename), line_start, line_end]; a report matches when the frames (inlined-at frames included) of its two pcs hit A and B in either order, within +-tol lines (default 2). role: primary = the oracle's pair; family = the same statements the oracle says conflict in the same way; extra = the oracle's extra_pairs/additional_pairs; both_builds = pairs the review says are present in both builds and unrelated to the fix. fixed.equiv = the buggy pair at the fixed build's line numbers (a report on it = STILL-REPORTED); fixed.residual = the oracle's residual pairs (a report = RESIDUAL-AS-EXPECTED). cls = the class the oracle pre-registers for the pair.

_t21c_doc: T21c additions (same format as above). Derived by hand from the reviewed oracle files eval/realworld/oracle/<id>.json (sites, other_conflicting_accesses / additional_pairs, thread_relation, expected_class, buggy_expected, class_reason, review.notes) and checked line by line against the source that was compiled (R2: eval/realworld/targets/<id>/r2/buggy/<path>; R1: git show <pinned>:<path>). role here: primary = the oracle's registered `sites`; family = further instances the oracle's buggy_expected lists as expected reports (same statements, other kernel/copy/step); extra = pairs the oracle names only in other_conflicting_accesses or additional_pairs (they only keep a report out of the 'other reports' queue; for DR+SC targets every cls=SC pair counts for the SC component, so SC additional_pairs score as '(family)' by the scorer's labelling). No pair was added from a detector report. Candidates have no fixed build except llamacpp-open-2 (fixed 99db719bdf07, oracle review.changes: expected_fixed_build_if_moved_to_recall = absent for the pair).

miss_cause.llamacpp-open-2-buggy: m1: the loop-carried WAR needs a second iteration of the k_VKQ_0 loop (fattn-vec.cuh L254) inside one CTA, and the driver's launch gives each CTA exactly one: the kernel JSONs show grid_cta_count 16 x 128 threads (4 heads x parallel_blocks 4), launch_fattn (fattn-common.cuh L1193-1218) sets parallel_blocks = min(max_blocks_per_sm, ntiles_KV) and then raises it up to ntiles_KV = 512/128 = 4 (nbatch_fa = D = 128, fattn-vec.cuh L541), so the loop stride gridDim.y*128 = 512 = kv. The only verdicts between the oracle's sites are the RAW L303 -> L359 (ORDERED, barrier-ordered by the __syncwarp at L320), which the oracle says must not be reported; there is no WAR verdict (neither ORDERED nor RACE). Driver fix needed (T21a): more KV tiles than parallel_blocks covers (a much longer kv, or more heads so that fewer parallel blocks are chosen), then rerun
